sv5.name: Scyther
sv5.effect: The sharp scythes on its forearms become increasingly sharp by cutting through hard objects.

sv5.name: Pineco
sv5.effect: It spits out a fluid that it uses to glue tree bark to its body. The fluid hardens when it touches air.

sv5.name: Seedot
sv5.effect: If it remains still, it looks just like a real nut. It delights in surprising foraging Pokémon.

sv5.name: Nuzleaf
sv5.effect: It lives deep in forests. With the leaf on its head, it makes a flute whose song makes listeners uneasy.

sv5.name: Shiftry
sv5.effect: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.

sv5.name: Shroomish
sv5.effect: If it senses danger, it scatters spores from the top of its head to protect itself.

sv5.name: Breloom
sv5.effect: The seeds on its tail are made of toxic spores. It knocks out foes with quick, virtually invisible punches.

sv5.name: Roselia
sv5.effect: Its flowers give off a relaxing fragrance. The stronger its aroma, the healthier the Roselia is.

sv5.name: Roserade
sv5.effect: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.

sv5.name: Turtwig
sv5.effect: Photosynthesis occurs across its body under the sun. The shell on its back is actually hardened soil.

sv5.name: Grotle
sv5.effect: It lives along water in forests. In the daytime, it leaves the forest to sunbathe its treed shell.

sv5.name: Torterra ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Shaymin
sv5.effect: It can dissolve toxins in the air to instantly transform ruined land into a lush field of flowers.

sv5.name: Cottonee
sv5.effect: It shoots cotton from its body to protect itself. If it gets caught up in hurricane-strength winds, it can get sent to the other side of the Earth.

sv5.name: Whimsicott
sv5.effect: It scatters cotton all over the place as a prank. If it gets wet, it'll become too heavy to move and have no choice but to answer for its mischief.

sv5.name: Deerling
sv5.effect: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In this form, Deerling have a softly sweet scent that lingers in the nose.

sv5.name: Sawsbuck
sv5.effect: Sawsbuck in their Autumn Form are known for having very short tempers. The males fight each other incessantly.

sv5.name: Grubbin
sv5.effect: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.

sv5.name: Dhelmise
sv5.effect: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.

sv5.name: Bramblin
sv5.effect: Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.

sv5.name: Brambleghast
sv5.effect: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.

sv5.name: Scovillain ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Rellor
sv5.effect: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

sv5.name: Rabsca
sv5.effect: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.

sv5.name: Iron Leaves ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Ponyta
sv5.effect: It can't run properly when it's newly born. As it races around with others of its kind, its legs grow stronger.

sv5.name: Rapidash
sv5.effect: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

sv5.name: Slugma
sv5.effect: A common sight in volcanic areas, it slowly slithers around in a constant search for warm places.

sv5.name: Magcargo
sv5.effect: Its brittle shell occasionally spouts intense flames that circulate throughout its body.

sv5.name: Victini
sv5.effect: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

sv5.name: Heatmor
sv5.effect: There's a hole in its tail that allows it to draw in the air it needs to keep its fire burning. If the hole gets blocked, this Pokémon will fall ill.

sv5.name: Litten
sv5.effect: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.

sv5.name: Torracat
sv5.effect: In the midst of battle, the fire pouch on Torracat's neck rings like a bell and produces stronger flames than usual.

sv5.name: Incineroar ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Turtonator
sv5.effect: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

sv5.name: Sizzlipede
sv5.effect: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

sv5.name: Centiskorch
sv5.effect: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

sv5.name: Gouging Fire ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Totodile
sv5.effect: It is small but rough and tough. It won't hesitate to take a bite out of anything that moves.

sv5.name: Croconaw
sv5.effect: If it loses a fang, a new one grows back in its place. There are always 48 fangs lining its mouth.

sv5.name: Feraligatr
sv5.effect: It usually moves slowly, but it goes at blinding speed when it attacks and bites prey.

sv5.name: Carvanha
sv5.effect: It won't attack while it's alone—not even if it spots prey. Instead, it waits for other Carvanha to join it, and then the Pokémon attack as a group.

sv5.name: Sharpedo
sv5.effect: As soon as it catches the scent of prey, Sharpedo will jet seawater from its backside, hurtling toward the target to attack at 75 mph.

sv5.name: Keldeo
sv5.effect: Keldeo has strengthened its resolve for battle, filling its body with power and changing its form.

sv5.name: Snom
sv5.effect: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.

sv5.name: Frosmoth
sv5.effect: Frosmoth senses air currents with its antennae. It sends its scales drifting on frigid air, making them fall like snow.

sv5.name: Wiglett
sv5.effect: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

sv5.name: Finizen
sv5.effect: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

sv5.name: Palafin
sv5.effect: This Pokémon's ancient genes have awakened. It is now so extraordinarily strong that it can easily lift a cruise ship with one fin.

sv5.name: Walking Wake ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Pikachu
sv5.effect: When several of these Pokémon gather, their electricity can build and cause lightning storms.

sv5.name: Raichu
sv5.effect: If the electric pouches in its cheeks become fully charged, both ears will stand straight up.

sv5.name: Electabuzz
sv5.effect: Many power plants keep Ground-type Pokémon around as a defense against Electabuzz that come seeking electricity.

sv5.name: Electivire
sv5.effect: The amount of electrical energy this Pokémon produces is proportional to the rate of its pulse. The voltage jumps while Electivire is battling.

sv5.name: Charjabug
sv5.effect: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.

sv5.name: Vikavolt
sv5.effect: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.

sv5.name: Zeraora
sv5.effect: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.

sv5.name: Yamper
sv5.effect: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

sv5.name: Boltund
sv5.effect: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

sv5.name: Wugtrio ex
sv5.effect: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's). Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards. Tera: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).

sv5.name: Iron Hands
sv5.effect: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

sv5.name: Iron Thorns
sv5.effect: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

sv5.name: Mr. Mime
sv5.effect: The broadness of its hands may be no coincidence—many scientists believe its palms became enlarged specifically for pantomiming.

sv5.name: Marill
sv5.effect: The fur on its body naturally repels water. It can stay dry even when it plays in the water.

sv5.name: Azumarill
sv5.effect: Its long ears are superb sensors. It can distinguish the movements of things in water and tell what they are.

sv5.name: Girafarig
sv5.effect: Girafarig's tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.

sv5.name: Latias
sv5.effect: It communicates using telepathy. Its body is covered in down that refracts light to make it invisible.

sv5.name: Bronzor
sv5.effect: Ancient people believed that the pattern on Bronzor's back contained a mysterious power.

sv5.name: Bronzong
sv5.effect: In ages past, this Pokémon was revered as a bringer of rain. It was found buried in the ground.

sv5.name: Solosis
sv5.effect: It communicates with others telepathically. Its body is encapsulated in liquid, but if it takes a heavy blow, the liquid will leak out.

sv5.name: Duosion
sv5.effect: Its psychic power can supposedly cover a range of more than half a mile—but only if its two brains can agree with each other.

sv5.name: Reuniclus
sv5.effect: While it could use its psychic abilities in battle, this Pokémon prefers to swing its powerful arms around to beat opponents into submission.

sv5.name: Elgyem
sv5.effect: If this Pokémon stands near a TV, strange scenery will appear on the screen. That scenery is said to be from its home.

sv5.name: Beheeyem
sv5.effect: Whenever a Beheeyem visits a farm, a Dubwool mysteriously disappears.

sv5.name: Cutiefly
sv5.effect: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur's pollen.

sv5.name: Ribombee
sv5.effect: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs' effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.

sv5.name: Scream Tail
sv5.effect: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.

sv5.name: Flutter Mane
sv5.effect: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.

sv5.name: Iron Valiant
sv5.effect: It's possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

sv5.name: Iron Valiant
sv5.effect: It's possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

sv5.name: Iron Crown ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Meditite
sv5.effect: It meditates to heighten its inner energy and to float in the air. It eats one berry a day.

sv5.name: Medicham
sv5.effect: It elegantly avoids attacks with dance-like steps, then launches a devastating blow in the same motion.

sv5.name: Relicanth
sv5.effect: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.

sv5.name: Drilbur
sv5.effect: It brings its claws together and whirls around at high speed before rushing toward its prey.

sv5.name: Excadrill
sv5.effect: It's not uncommon for tunnels that appear to have formed naturally to actually be a result of Excadrill's rampant digging.

sv5.name: Golett
sv5.effect: They were sculpted from clay in ancient times. No one knows why, but some of them are driven to continually line up boulders.

sv5.name: Golurk
sv5.effect: Artillery platforms built into the walls of ancient castles served as perches from which Golurk could fire energy beams.

sv5.name: Rockruff
sv5.effect: This Pokémon is very friendly when it's young. Its disposition becomes vicious once it matures, but it never forgets the kindness of its master.

sv5.name: Lycanroc
sv5.effect: Lycanroc attacks its prey with its sharp claws and fangs. It loyally obeys the instructions of a Trainer it trusts.

sv5.name: Mudbray
sv5.effect: This Pokémon covers itself in mud that it has regurgitated. The mud won't dry out even if it's exposed to the sun for a long time.

sv5.name: Mudsdale
sv5.effect: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.

sv5.name: Rolycoly
sv5.effect: On sunny days, Rolycoly will come out onto grassy plains and roll around. Then it will eat the grass that gets tangled in its wheel-like leg.

sv5.name: Carkol
sv5.effect: The temperature inside its body increases when it experiences strong emotions. It rolls around frantically while spewing flames.

sv5.name: Coalossal
sv5.effect: To intimidate its opponents, Coalossal will vigorously shake its body, scattering coal from its smoldering back.

sv5.name: Great Tusk
sv5.effect: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

sv5.name: Great Tusk
sv5.effect: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

sv5.name: Sandy Shocks
sv5.effect: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon's traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

sv5.name: Iron Boulder ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Ekans
sv5.effect: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

sv5.name: Arbok
sv5.effect: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.

sv5.name: Gastly
sv5.effect: It wraps its opponent in its gas-like body, slowly weakening its prey by poisoning it through the skin.

sv5.name: Haunter
sv5.effect: It likes to lurk in the dark and tap shoulders with a gaseous hand. Its touch causes endless shuddering.

sv5.name: Gengar ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Poochyena
sv5.effect: A Pokémon with a persistent nature, it chases its chosen prey until the prey becomes exhausted.

sv5.name: Mightyena
sv5.effect: It will always obey the commands of a skilled Trainer. Its behavior arises from its living in packs in ancient times.

sv5.name: Sableye
sv5.effect: It dwells in the darkness of caves. It uses its sharp claws to dig up gems to nourish itself.

sv5.name: Farigiraf ex
sv5.effect: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's). Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards. Tera: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).

sv5.name: Roaring Moon
sv5.effect: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.

sv5.name: Forretress
sv5.effect: Its entire body is shielded by a steel-hard shell. What lurks inside this shell is a total mystery.

sv5.name: Scizor ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Mawile
sv5.effect: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.

sv5.name: Beldum
sv5.effect: From its rear, Beldum emits a magnetic force that rapidly pulls opponents in. They get skewered on Beldum's sharp claws.

sv5.name: Metang
sv5.effect: Two Beldum have become stuck together via their own magnetic forces. With two brains, the resulting Metang has doubled psychic powers.

sv5.name: Metagross
sv5.effect: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.

sv5.name: Meltan
sv5.effect: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

sv5.name: Melmetal
sv5.effect: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.

sv5.name: Iron Treads
sv5.effect: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

sv5.name: Koraidon
sv5.effect: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

sv5.name: Koraidon ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Miraidon
sv5.effect: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

sv5.name: Miraidon ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Raging Bolt ex
sv5.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv5.name: Lickitung
sv5.effect: If this Pokémon's sticky saliva gets on you and you don't clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won't go away, either.

sv5.name: Lickilicky
sv5.effect: Lickilicky's strange tongue can stretch to many times the length of its body. No one has figured out how Lickilicky's tongue can stretch so far.

sv5.name: Hoothoot
sv5.effect: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.

sv5.name: Noctowl
sv5.effect: Its eyes are specially developed to enable it to see clearly even in murky darkness and minimal light.

sv5.name: Dunsparce
sv5.effect: It creates mazes in dark locations. When spotted, it flees into the ground by digging with its tail.

sv5.name: Dudunsparce
sv5.effect: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

sv5.name: Skitty
sv5.effect: It can't stop itself from chasing moving things, and it runs in a circle, chasing its own tail.

sv5.name: Delcatty
sv5.effect: It dislikes dirty places. It often searches for a comfortable place in which to groom itself.

sv5.name: Chatot
sv5.effect: It mimics the cries of other Pokémon to trick them into thinking it's one of them. This way they won't attack it.

sv5.name: Pidove
sv5.effect: Where people go, these Pokémon follow. If you're scattering food for them, be careful— several hundred of them can gather at once.

sv5.name: Tranquill
sv5.effect: It can fly moderately quickly. No matter how far it travels, it can always find its way back to its master and its nest.

sv5.name: Unfezant
sv5.effect: Unfezant are exceptional fliers. The females are known for their stamina, while the males outclass them in terms of speed.

sv5.name: Minccino
sv5.effect: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.

sv5.name: Cinccino
sv5.effect: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.

sv5.name: Drampa
sv5.effect: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

sv5.name: Iron Jugulis
sv5.effect: It's possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

sv5.name: Ancient Booster Energy Capsule
sv5.effect: The Ancient Pokémon this card is attached to gets +60 HP, recovers from all Special Conditions, and can't be affected by any Special Conditions. You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

sv5.name: Awakening Drum
sv5.effect: Draw a card for each of your Ancient Pokémon in play. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn. ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

sv5.name: Bianca's Devotion
sv5.effect: Heal all damage from 1 of your Pokémon that has 30 HP or less remaining. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv5.effect: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv5.name: Ciphermaniac's Codebreaking
sv5.effect: Search your deck for 2 cards, shuffle your deck, then put those cards on top of it in any order. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv5.name: Eri
sv5.effect: Your opponent reveals their hand, and you discard up to 2 Item cards you find there. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv5.name: Explorer's Guidance
sv5.effect: Look at the top 6 cards of your deck and put 2 of them into your hand. Discard the other cards. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv5.name: Full Metal Lab

You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it into the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

sv5.name: Future Booster Energy Capsule

You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

sv5.name: Hand Trimmer
sv5.effect: Each player discards cards from their hand until they have 5 cards in their hand. Your opponent discards first. (If a player has 5 or fewer cards in their hand, they do not discard.) You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv5.name: Heavy Baton
sv5.effect: If the Pokémon this card is attached to has a Retreat Cost of exactly 4, is in the Active Spot, and is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, move up to 3 Basic Energy cards from that Pokémon to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like. You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

sv5.name: Hero's Cape
sv5.effect: The Pokémon this card is attached to gets +100 HP. You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached. ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

sv5.name: Master Ball
sv5.effect: Search your deck for a Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn. ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

sv5.name: Maximum Belt
sv5.effect: Attacks used by the Pokémon this card is attached to do 50 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon ex (before applying Weakness and Resistance). You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached. ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

sv5.name: Morty's Conviction
sv5.effect: You can use this card only if you discard another card from your hand.  Draw a card for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv5.name: Perilous Jungle

sv5.name: Cutiefly

sv5.name: Excadrill

sv5.name: Mudsdale

sv5.name: Lickitung

sv6.name: Tangrowth
sv6.effect: Tangrowth has two arms that it can extend as it pleases. Recent research has shown that these arms are, in fact, bundles of vines.

sv6.name: Pinsir
sv6.effect: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.

sv6.name: Spinarak
sv6.effect: Some fishers weave its sturdy thread into nets to catch fish Pokémon.

sv6.name: Ariados
sv6.effect: It wanders in search of food after darkness falls, never nesting in a specific place.

sv6.name: Sunkern
sv6.effect: It is very weak. Its only means of defense is to shake its leaves desperately at its attacker.

sv6.name: Sunflora
sv6.effect: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.

sv6.name: Heracross
sv6.effect: With its herculean powers, it can easily throw around an object that is 100 times its own weight.

sv6.name: Volbeat
sv6.effect: It flashes the light on its rear to communicate with other Volbeat. It loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.

sv6.name: Illumise
sv6.effect: It guides Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. There are scholars who research the meaning of these signs.

sv6.name: Leafeon
sv6.effect: The younger they are, the more they smell like fresh grass. With age, their fragrance takes on the odor of fallen leaves.

sv6.name: Phantump
sv6.effect: This Pokémon came to be when the spirit of a deceased child possessed a tree stump. It now wanders the forest searching for friends.

sv6.name: Trevenant
sv6.effect: Trevenant is very kind to Pokémon living in the forest. It doesn't even care if these Pokémon take up residence in the greenery on its head.

sv6.name: Grookey
sv6.effect: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.

sv6.name: Thwackey
sv6.effect: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

sv6.name: Rillaboom
sv6.effect: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

sv6.name: Applin
sv6.effect: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

sv6.name: Dipplin
sv6.effect: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

sv6.name: Iron Leaves
sv6.effect: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

sv6.name: Poltchageist

sv6.name: Monferno
sv6.effect: It skillfully controls the intensity of the fire on its tail to keep its foes at an ideal distance.

sv6.name: Infernape
sv6.effect: Its crown of fire is indicative of its fiery nature. It is beaten by none in terms of quickness.

sv6.name: Darumaka
sv6.effect: It derives its power from fire burning inside its body. If the fire dwindles, this Pokémon will immediately fall asleep.

sv6.name: Darmanitan
sv6.effect: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

sv6.name: Litwick
sv6.effect: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life-force of any who follow it.

sv6.name: Lampent
sv6.effect: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

sv6.name: Chandelure
sv6.effect: It absorbs spirits, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

sv6.name: Chi-Yu
sv6.effect: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

sv6.name: Poliwhirl
sv6.effect: Its skin is moist all over its body. The skin on its belly spiral also feels smooth.

sv6.name: Poliwrath
sv6.effect: It can use its well-developed arms and legs to run on the surface of the water for a split second.

sv6.name: Goldeen
sv6.effect: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.

sv6.name: Seaking
sv6.effect: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

sv6.name: Jynx
sv6.effect: In certain parts of Galar, Jynx was once feared and worshiped as the Queen of Ice.

sv6.name: Corphish
sv6.effect: It can live in impure water, where it doesn't need to compete with other water Pokémon for food, so its numbers have steadily increased.

sv6.name: Crawdaunt
sv6.effect: A rough customer that wildly flails its giant claws. It is said to be extremely hard to raise.

sv6.name: Feebas
sv6.effect: It is the shabbiest Pokémon of all. It forms schools and lives at the bottom of rivers that teem with plant life.

sv6.name: Milotic
sv6.effect: It lives at the bottom of clear lakes. In times of war, it shows itself, which soothes people's minds and hearts.

sv6.name: Snorunt
sv6.effect: It is said that a home visited by a Snorunt will prosper. It can withstand cold of −150 degrees Fahrenheit.

sv6.name: Glalie
sv6.effect: It prevents prey from escaping by instantaneously freezing moisture in the air.

sv6.name: Froslass
sv6.effect: It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.

sv6.name: Glaceon
sv6.effect: It lowers its body heat to freeze its fur. The hairs then become like needles it can fire.

sv6.name: Phione
sv6.effect: When the water warms, they inflate the flotation sac on their heads and drift languidly on the sea in packs.

sv6.name: Froakie
sv6.effect: It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.

sv6.name: Frogadier
sv6.effect: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.

sv6.name: Cramorant
sv6.effect: It's an incredibly poor learner because it uses the bare minimum amount of energy for its brain. It focuses on battling instead.

sv6.name: Finizen
sv6.effect: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

sv6.name: Palafin
sv6.effect: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen's, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

sv6.name: Shinx

sv6.name: Helioptile
sv6.effect: When spread, the frills on its head act like solar panels, generating the power behind this Pokémon's electric moves.

sv6.name: Heliolisk
sv6.effect: A now-vanished desert culture treasured these Pokémon. Appropriately, when Heliolisk came to the Galar region, treasure came with them.

sv6.name: Morpeko
sv6.effect: It has a small stomach. If it isn't constantly eating the seeds it keeps in its pockets, it will get hungry immediately.

sv6.name: Tadbulb
sv6.effect: It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground.

sv6.name: Bellibolt
sv6.effect: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt's belly-button dynamo.

sv6.name: Wattrel
sv6.effect: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they're a popular delicacy.

sv6.name: Kilowattrel
sv6.effect: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There's hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.

sv6.name: Iron Thorns ex
sv6.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv6.name: Clefairy
sv6.effect: On nights with a full moon, they gather together and dance. The surrounding area is enveloped in an abnormal magnetic field.

sv6.name: Clefable
sv6.effect: It has an acute sense of hearing. It can easily hear a pin being dropped nearly 1,100 yards away.

sv6.name: Abra
sv6.effect: This Pokémon uses its psychic powers while it sleeps. The contents of Abra's dreams affect the powers that the Pokémon wields.

sv6.name: Kadabra
sv6.effect: Using its psychic power, Kadabra levitates as it sleeps. It uses its springy tail as a pillow.

sv6.name: Alakazam
sv6.effect: It has an incredibly high level of intelligence. Some say that Alakazam remembers everything that ever happens to it, from birth till death.

sv6.name: Girafarig
sv6.effect: Girafarig's tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.

sv6.name: Farigiraf
sv6.effect: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

sv6.name: Chimecho
sv6.effect: Its cries echo inside its hollow body to emerge as beautiful notes for startling and repelling foes.

sv6.name: Flabébé
sv6.effect: This Flabébé rides a red flower. Immediately after birth, this Pokémon begins flying around in search of a flower it likes.

sv6.name: Floette
sv6.effect: This Pokémon uses red wavelengths of light to pour its own energy into flowers and draw forth their latent potential.

sv6.name: Florges
sv6.effect: They say that flower gardens created by Florges are constantly showered with a power that can heal both body and spirit.

sv6.name: Swirlix
sv6.effect: It eats its own weight in sugar every day. If it doesn't get enough sugar, it becomes incredibly grumpy.

sv6.name: Slurpuff
sv6.effect: By taking in a person's scent, it can sniff out their mental and physical condition. It's hoped that this skill will have many medical applications.

sv6.name: Sandygast
sv6.effect: It flings sand into the eyes of its prey and tries to close in on them while they're blinded, but since Sandygast is so slow, the prey tends to escape.

sv6.name: Palossand
sv6.effect: From the hollows in its arms, it fires the bones of its victims, which are all dried up after being drained of their vitality.

sv6.name: Enamorus

sv6.name: Fezandipiti

sv6.name: Sandshrew

sv6.name: Sandslash
sv6.effect: The spikes on its body are made up of its hardened hide. It rolls up and attacks foes with its spikes.

sv6.name: Hisuian Growlithe

sv6.name: Hisuian Arcanine

sv6.name: Nosepass

sv6.name: Probopass

sv6.name: Timburr

sv6.name: Gurdurr
sv6.effect: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

sv6.name: Conkeldurr

sv6.effect: Glimmora's petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.

sv6.name: Ting-Lu
sv6.effect: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

sv6.name: Okidogi
sv6.effect: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

sv6.name: Poochyena
sv6.effect: Poochyena pursue their prey in packs. Once the prey is exhausted, the pack finishes it off. But sometimes the prey retaliates, and the pack flees.

sv6.name: Mightyena
sv6.effect: Once it's caught the scent of faraway prey, the leader gives a signal, and the whole pack moves out.

sv6.name: Venipede
sv6.effect: Venipede and Sizzlipede are similar species, but when the two meet, a huge fight ensues.

sv6.name: Whirlipede
sv6.effect: This Pokémon spins itself rapidly and charges into its opponents. Its top speed is just over 60 mph.

sv6.name: Scolipede
sv6.effect: Scolipede latches on to its prey with the claws on its neck before slamming them into the ground and jabbing them with its claws' toxic spikes.

sv6.name: Brute Bonnet
sv6.effect: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.

sv6.name: Skarmory
sv6.effect: People fashion swords from Skarmory's shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.

sv6.name: Aron
sv6.effect: It eats iron ore—and sometimes railroad tracks— to build up the steel armor that protects its body.

sv6.name: Lairon
sv6.effect: Lairon live in mountains brimming with spring water and iron ore, so these Pokémon often came into conflict with humans in the past.

sv6.name: Aggron
sv6.effect: Aggron has a horn sharp enough to perforate thick iron sheets. It brings down its opponents by ramming into them horn first.

sv6.name: Heatran
sv6.effect: It dwells in volcanic caves. It digs in with its cross-shaped feet to crawl on ceilings and walls.

sv6.name: Varoom
sv6.effect: The steel section is Varoom's actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.

sv6.name: Revavroom
sv6.effect: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.

sv6.name: Applin
sv6.effect: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

sv6.name: Dipplin
sv6.effect: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

sv6.name: Dreepy
sv6.effect: It has a habit of biting at Clauncher even though it doesn't feed on them. This is said to be vestigial behavior from when Dreepy was alive.

sv6.name: Drakloak
sv6.effect: This Pokémon stores up energy in its lungs, then shoots it out. It takes care of Dreepy and battles alongside them until they're all grown up.

sv6.name: Farfetch'd
sv6.effect: The stalk this Pokémon carries in its wings serves as a sword to cut down opponents. In a dire situation, the stalk can also serve as food.

sv6.name: Chansey
sv6.effect: It walks carefully to prevent its egg from breaking. However, it is extremely fast at running away.

sv6.name: Blissey ex

sv6.name: Eevee
sv6.effect: Its genetic code is irregular. It may mutate if it is exposed to radiation from element stones.

sv6.name: Snorlax
sv6.effect: Its stomach's digestive juices can dissolve any kind of poison. Eating things off the ground doesn't bother it at all.

sv6.name: Aipom
sv6.effect: Its tail moves with greater dexterity than its hands. Making deft use of this tail, Aipom lives high among the treetops.

sv6.name: Ambipom
sv6.effect: Split into two, the tails are so adept at handling and doing things that Ambipom rarely uses its hands.

sv6.name: Ducklett
sv6.effect: It strengthens its body by diving into the depths of ponds, swimming around while looking for bog moss to eat.

sv6.name: Swanna

sv7.name: Toedscool

sv8.name: Vivillon

sv8.name: Morelull

sv8.name: Shiinotic

sv8.name: Dhelmise

sv8.name: Zarude

sv8.name: Capsakid

sv8.name: Rellor
sv8.effect: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

sv8.name: Rabsca

sv8.name: Wo-Chien
sv8.effect: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.

sv8.name: Vulpix
sv8.effect: As its body grows larger, its six warm tails become more beautiful, with a more luxurious coat of fur.

sv8.name: Ninetales
sv8.effect: It has nine long tails and fur that gleams gold. It is said to live for 1,000 years.

sv8.name: Paldean Tauros
sv8.effect: People call this kind of Tauros the Blaze Breed due to the hot air it snorts from its nostrils. Its three tails are intertwined.

sv8.name: Ho-Oh
sv8.effect: A legend says that its body glows in seven colors. A rainbow is said to form behind it when it flies.

sv8.name: Castform Sunny Form
sv8.effect: This is the form Castform takes on bright days. In an experiment where Castform was placed in front of a heater, it didn't change to this form.

sv8.name: Victini
sv8.effect: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

sv8.name: Pansear
sv8.effect: Very intelligent, it roasts berries before eating them. It likes to help people.

sv8.name: Simisear
sv8.effect: A flame burns inside its body. It scatters embers from its head and tail to sear its opponents.

sv8.name: Larvesta

sv8.name: Volcarona

sv8.name: Oricorio
sv8.effect: This form of Oricorio has sipped red nectar. It whips up blazing flames as it moves to the steps of its passionate dance.

sv8.name: Sizzlipede

sv8.name: Centiskorch
sv8.effect: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

sv8.name: Fuecoco
sv8.effect: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco's head and flickers to and fro.

sv8.name: Crocalor

sv8.name: Skeledirge

sv8.name: Charcadet
sv8.effect: Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat.

sv8.name: Mantine

sv8.name: Azumarill

sv8.name: Mesprit

sv8.name: Azelf

sv8.name: Cofagrigus

sv8.name: Espurr

sv8.name: Oricorio

sv8.name: Sandygast

sv8.name: Flittle

sv8.name: Espathra

sv8.name: Flutter Mane

sv8.name: Gimmighoul

sv8.name: Mankey

sv8.name: Primeape

sv8.name: Annihilape

sv8.name: Paldean Tauros

sv8.name: Phanpy

sv8.name: Donphan

sv8.name: Trapinch

sv8.name: Vibrava

sv8.name: Drilbur
sv8.effect: It makes its way swiftly through the soil by putting both claws together and rotating at high speed.

sv8.name: Excadrill

sv8.name: Landorus
sv8.effect: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”

sv8.name: Passimian
sv8.effect: The boss chooses 10 members of the group to go out hunting. The hunting party will evenly split the food they find with the rest of the group.

sv8.name: Clobbopus
sv8.effect: It's very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

sv8.name: Grapploct

sv8.name: Glimmet

sv8.name: Glimmora

sv8.name: Koraidon
sv8.effect: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

sv8.name: Deino

sv8.name: Zweilous

sv8.name: Hydreigon ex

sv8.name: Grafaiai

sv8.name: Alolan Diglett

sv8.name: Alolan Dugtrio
sv8.effect: Its metallic whiskers are heavy, so it's not very fast, but it has the power to dig through bedrock.

sv8.name: Skarmory
sv8.effect: Since the feathers that it sheds are thin and sharp, people apparently once used them as swords.

sv8.name: Registeel

sv8.name: Bronzor

sv8.name: Bronzong

sv8.name: Klefki

sv8.name: Duraludon

sv10.effect: It likes to make its shell thicker by adding layers of tree bark. The additional weight doesn't bother it.

sv10.name: Shroomish
sv10.effect: It prefers damp places. By day it remains still in the forest shade. It releases toxic powder from its head.

sv10.name: Breloom
sv10.effect: It scatters poisonous spores and throws powerful punches while its foe is hampered by inhaled spores.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Roselia

sv10.name: Cynthia's Roserade
sv10.effect: The poison in its right hand is quick acting. The poison in its left hand is slow acting. Both are life threatening.

sv10.name: Mow Rotom
sv10.effect: The lawn mower is one of the household appliances that led to the development of the Rotom Dex.

sv10.name: Shaymin
sv10.effect: The blooming of Gracidea flowers confers the power of flight upon it. Feelings of gratitude are the message it delivers.

sv10.name: Dwebble
sv10.effect: It first tries to find a rock to live in, but if there are no suitable rocks to be found, Dwebble may move in to the ports of a Hippowdon.

sv10.name: Crustle
sv10.effect: Its thick claws are its greatest weapons. They're mighty enough to crack Rhyperior's carapace.

sv10.name: Fomantis
sv10.effect: Fomantis hates having its naps interrupted. It fires off beams using energy it gathers by bathing in the sun.

sv10.name: Lurantis
sv10.effect: By masquerading as a bug Pokémon, it lowers the guard of actual bug Pokémon lured in by a scent of sweet flowers. Its sickles bring them down.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Blipbug
sv10.effect: Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.

sv10.name: Applin
sv10.effect: It grows by eating the flesh of an apple. Applin uses its own body fluid to strengthen the apple's skin and prevent it from rotting.

sv10.name: Dipplin
sv10.effect: Dipplin is two creatures in one Pokémon. Its evolution was triggered by a special apple grown only in one place.

sv10.name: Hydrapple
sv10.effect: Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Tarountula
sv10.effect: The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon's natural enemy.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Spidops
sv10.effect: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

sv10.name: Smoliv
sv10.effect: It protects itself from enemies by emitting oil from the fruit on its head. This oil is bitter and astringent enough to make someone flinch.

sv10.name: Dolliv
sv10.effect: Dolliv shares its tasty, fresh-scented oil with others. This species has coexisted with humans since times long gone.

sv10.name: Arboliva ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Rellor
sv10.effect: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

sv10.name: Growlithe

sv10.name: Arcanine
sv10.effect: An ancient picture scroll shows that people were captivated by its movement as it ran through prairies.

sv10.name: Ponyta
sv10.effect: If you've been accepted by Ponyta, its burning mane is mysteriously no longer hot to the touch.

sv10.name: Rapidash
sv10.effect: The fastest runner becomes the leader, and it decides the herd's pace and direction of travel.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Moltres ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Ethan's Cyndaquil
sv10.effect: It usually stays hunched over. If it is angry or surprised, it shoots flames out of its back.

sv10.name: Ethan's Quilava
sv10.effect: Before battle, it turns its back on its opponent to demonstrate how ferociously its fire blazes.

sv10.name: Ethan's Typhlosion
sv10.effect: It has a secret, devastating move. It rubs its blazing fur to cause huge explosions.

sv10.name: Ethan's Slugma
sv10.effect: Its lava body can cool and chip away at times, but a magma bath will heal it right up.

sv10.name: Ethan's Magcargo
sv10.effect: This Pokémon lives near the craters of volcanoes. It stores fire energy in its shell of cooled and hardened magma.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Houndour
sv10.effect: It is smart enough to hunt in packs. It uses a variety of cries for communicating with others.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Houndoom
sv10.effect: If you are burned by the flames it shoots from its mouth, the pain will never go away.

sv10.name: Ethan's Ho-Oh ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Torchic
sv10.effect: Torchic feels toasty warm if you hug it. It has a flame sac inside its belly, and the flames burn continuously as long as Torchic has life in it.

sv10.name: Combusken
sv10.effect: It boosts its concentration by emitting harsh cries. Its kicks have outstanding destructive power.

sv10.name: Blaziken
sv10.effect: When facing a tough foe, it looses flames from its wrists. Its powerful legs let it jump clear over buildings.

sv10.name: Heat Rotom
sv10.effect: If the convection microwave oven is not working properly, then the Rotom inhabiting it will become lethargic.

sv10.name: Hearthflame Mask Ogerpon
sv10.effect: This form is the most aggressive, bombarding enemies with the intensity of flames blazing within a hearth.

sv10.name: Misty's Psyduck
sv10.effect: It is constantly wracked by a headache. When the headache turns intense, it begins using mysterious powers.

sv10.name: Misty's Staryu
sv10.effect: Fish Pokémon nibble at it, but Staryu isn't bothered. Its body regenerates quickly, even if part of it is completely torn off.

sv10.name: Misty's Starmie
sv10.effect: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.

sv10.name: Misty's Magikarp
sv10.effect: An underpowered, pathetic Pokémon. It may jump high on rare occasions but never more than seven feet.

sv10.name: Misty's Gyarados
sv10.effect: Once it appears, it goes on a rampage. It remains enraged until it demolishes everything around it.

sv10.name: Misty's Lapras
sv10.effect: It ferries people across the sea on its back. It may sing an enchanting cry if it is in a good mood.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Articuno
sv10.effect: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Feebas
sv10.effect: This tough Pokémon is perfectly fine even in dirty water. However, due to its ragged, shabby appearance, it isn't popular.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Milotic
sv10.effect: Its lovely scales are described as rainbow colored. They change color depending on the viewing angle.

sv10.name: Clamperl
sv10.effect: Clamperl's pearls are exceedingly precious. They can be more than 10 times as costly as Shellder's pearls.

sv10.name: Huntail
sv10.effect: Deep seas are their habitat. According to tradition, when Huntail wash up onshore, something unfortunate will happen.

sv10.name: Gorebyss
sv10.effect: It sucks bodily fluids out of its prey. The leftover meat sinks to the seafloor, where it becomes food for other Pokémon.

sv10.name: Buizel
sv10.effect: It spins its two tails like a screw to propel itself through water. The tails also slice clinging seaweed.

sv10.name: Floatzel
sv10.effect: With its flotation sac inflated, it can carry people on its back. It deflates the sac before it dives.

sv10.name: Snover
sv10.effect: During cold seasons, it migrates to the mountain's lower reaches. It returns to the snow-covered summit in the spring.

sv10.name: Abomasnow
sv10.effect: It lives a quiet life on mountains that are perpetually covered in snow. It hides itself by whipping up blizzards.

sv10.name: Wash Rotom
sv10.effect: This Rotom has entered a washing machine. It nods with satisfaction after it floods the surrounding area.

sv10.name: Arrokuda
sv10.effect: Arrokuda can swim quickly only in a straight line. The ones that become sluggish from overeating are the first to be targeted by flocks of Wattrel.

sv10.name: Barraskewda
sv10.effect: It spins its tail fins to leap from the water, then viciously bites down on Wingull flying close to the water's surface.

sv10.name: Cetoddle
sv10.effect: This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.

sv10.name: Cetitan ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Dondozo ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Wellspring Mask Ogerpon
sv10.effect: This form excels in both attack and defense. It ceaselessly unleashes moves like a spring gushes water.

sv10.name: Electabuzz
sv10.effect: Its body constantly discharges electricity. Getting close to it will make your hair stand on end.

sv10.name: Electivire ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Zapdos
sv10.effect: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It's said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.

sv10.name: Ethan's Pichu
sv10.effect: It is unskilled at storing electric power. Any kind of shock causes it to discharge energy spontaneously.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Mareep
sv10.effect: If static electricity builds in its body, its fleece doubles in volume. Touching it will shock you.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Flaaffy
sv10.effect: As a result of storing too much electricity, it developed patches where even downy wool won't grow.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Ampharos
sv10.effect: The bright light on its tail can be seen far away. It has been treasured since ancient times as a beacon.

sv10.name: Electrike
sv10.effect: It stores electricity in its fur. It gives off sparks from all over its body in seasons when the air is dry.

sv10.name: Manectric
sv10.effect: It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.

sv10.name: Rotom
sv10.effect: Its electricity-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.

sv10.name: Zeraora
sv10.effect: Electricity sparks from the pads on its limbs. Wherever Zeraora runs, lightning flashes and thunder echoes.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Drowzee
sv10.effect: It remembers every dream it eats. It rarely eats the dreams of adults because children's are much tastier.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Hypno
sv10.effect: When it locks eyes with an enemy, it will use a mix of psi moves, such as Hypnosis and Confusion.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Wobbuffet
sv10.effect: To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.

sv10.name: Steven's Baltoy
sv10.effect: It was discovered in ancient ruins. While moving, it constantly spins. It stands on one foot even when asleep.

sv10.name: Steven's Claydol
sv10.effect: It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Chingling
sv10.effect: There is an orb inside its mouth. When it hops, the orb bounces all over and makes a ringing sound.

sv10.name: Steven's Carbink
sv10.effect: It has slept underground for hundreds of millions of years since its birth. It's occasionally found during the excavation of caves.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Mimikyu
sv10.effect: This Pokémon lives in dark places untouched by sunlight. When it appears before humans, it hides itself under a cloth that resembles a Pikachu.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Dottler
sv10.effect: As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Orbeetle
sv10.effect: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what's around it—and what's around it can include things over six miles away.

sv10.name: Mankey
sv10.effect: It lives in groups in the treetops. If it loses sight of its group, it becomes infuriated by its loneliness.

sv10.name: Primeape
sv10.effect: It becomes wildly furious if it even senses someone looking at it. It chases anyone that meets its glare.

sv10.name: Annihilape
sv10.effect: When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.

sv10.name: Ethan's Sudowoodo
sv10.effect: Although it always pretends to be a tree, its composition appears more similar to rock than to vegetation.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Larvitar
sv10.effect: Born deep underground, this Pokémon becomes a pupa after eating enough dirt to make a mountain.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Pupitar
sv10.effect: This pupa flies around wildly by venting with great force the gas pressurized inside its body.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Tyranitar
sv10.effect: Extremely strong, it can change the landscape. It is so insolent that it doesn't care about others.

sv10.name: Nosepass
sv10.effect: The magnet in Nosepass's nose provides an unerring compass, making this Pokémon an excellent partner for Trainers going on a journey.

sv10.name: Probopass
sv10.effect: It controls three units called Mini-Noses using magnetic force. With them, it can attack a foe from three directions.

sv10.name: Meditite
sv10.effect: It never skips its daily yoga training. It heightens its inner strength through meditation.

sv10.name: Medicham
sv10.effect: Through yoga training, it gained the psychic power to predict its foe's next move.

sv10.name: Regirock ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Gible
sv10.effect: It skulks in caves, and when prey or an enemy passes by, it leaps out and chomps them. The force of its attack sometimes chips its teeth.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Gabite
sv10.effect: In rare cases, it molts and sheds its scales. Medicine containing its scales as an ingredient will make a weary body feel invigorated.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Garchomp ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Hippopotas
sv10.effect: It shrouds itself in sand to ward off germs. It travels easily through the sands of the desert.

sv10.name: Hippowdon
sv10.effect: It brandishes its gaping mouth in a display of fearsome strength. It raises vast quantities of sand while attacking.

sv10.name: Mudbray
sv10.effect: This Pokémon covers itself in mud that it has regurgitated. The mud won't dry out even if it's exposed to the sun for a long time.

sv10.name: Mudsdale
sv10.effect: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.

sv10.name: Arven's Toedscool
sv10.effect: Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.

sv10.name: Arven's Toedscruel
sv10.effect: These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.

sv10.name: Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon
sv10.effect: This form has excellent defenses, absorbing impacts solidly like the cornerstones that support houses.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Ekans
sv10.effect: It can freely detach its jaw to swallow large prey whole. It can become too heavy to move, however.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Arbok
sv10.effect: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Nidoran♀
sv10.effect: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran's horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male's horn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Nidorina
sv10.effect: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Nidoqueen
sv10.effect: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Nidoran♂
sv10.effect: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it's friendly with.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Nidorino
sv10.effect: It's nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Nidoking ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Zubat
sv10.effect: Zubat live in caves, down where the sun's light won't reach. In the morning, they gather together to keep each other warm as they sleep.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Golbat
sv10.effect: Its feet are tiny, but this Pokémon walks skillfully. It sneaks up on sleeping prey before sinking in its fangs and slurping up blood.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Crobat ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Grimer
sv10.effect: Born from sludge, these Pokémon now gather in polluted places and increase the bacteria in their bodies.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Muk
sv10.effect: It's thickly covered with a filthy, vile sludge. It is so toxic, even its footprints contain poison.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Koffing
sv10.effect: Toxic gas is held within its thin, balloon-shaped body, so it can cause massive explosions.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Weezing
sv10.effect: Top-grade perfume is made using its internal poison gases by diluting them to the highest level.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Murkrow
sv10.effect: Feared and loathed by many, it is believed to bring misfortune to all those who see it at night.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Sneasel
sv10.effect: This cunning Pokémon hides under the cover of darkness, waiting to attack its prey.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Spiritomb
sv10.effect: Its constant mischief and misdeeds resulted in it being bound to an Odd Keystone by a mysterious spell.

sv10.name: Marnie's Purrloin
sv10.effect: Opponents that get drawn in by its adorable behavior come away with stinging scratches from its claws and stinging pride from its laughter.

sv10.name: Marnie's Liepard
sv10.effect: This stealthy Pokémon sneaks up behind prey without making any sound at all. It competes with Thievul for territory.

sv10.name: Marnie's Scraggy
sv10.effect: It stretches its saggy skin up to its neck to protect itself. Among Scraggy, individuals with saggier skin apparently garner more respect.

sv10.name: Marnie's Scrafty
sv10.effect: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.

sv10.name: Marnie's Impidimp
sv10.effect: The reason this Pokémon causes trouble for those it feels close to is because Impidimp itself gets irritable if it can't absorb negative emotions.

sv10.name: Marnie's Morgrem
sv10.effect: Morgrem prefers dirty tactics, like ambushing, because it doesn't have confidence in its brawn.

sv10.name: Marnie's Grimmsnarl ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Marnie's Morpeko
sv10.effect: Morpeko eats seeds constantly to keep its hunger at bay. If it's hungry for too long, it grows wild and brutish.

sv10.name: Arven's Maschiff
sv10.effect: It always scowls in an attempt to make opponents take it seriously, but even crying children will burst into laughter when they see Maschiff's face.

sv10.name: Arven's Mabosstiff ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Forretress
sv10.effect: It's usually found hanging on to a fat tree trunk. It shoots out bits of its shell when it sees action.

sv10.name: Skarmory
sv10.effect: Its sturdy, heavy-looking iron body is actually thin and light, so it can fly at speeds over 180 mph.

sv10.name: Steven's Skarmory
sv10.effect: Its sturdy, heavy-looking iron body is actually thin and light, so it can fly at speeds over 180 mph.

sv10.name: Steven's Beldum
sv10.effect: The magnetic force generated by its body repels the ground's natural magnetism, letting it float.

sv10.name: Steven's Metang
sv10.effect: It is formed by two Beldum joining together. Its two brains are linked, amplifying its psychic power.

sv10.name: Steven's Metagross ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Zamazenta
sv10.effect: Its ability to deflect any attack led to it being known as the Fighting Master's Shield. It was feared and respected by all.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Rattata
sv10.effect: This Pokémon is common but hazardous. Its sharp incisors can easily cut right through hard wood.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Raticate
sv10.effect: Its whiskers are essential for maintaining its balance. No matter how friendly you are, it will get angry and bite you if you touch its whiskers.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Meowth
sv10.effect: All it does is sleep during the daytime. At night, it patrols its territory with its eyes aglow.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Persian ex
sv10.effect: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

sv10.name: Kangaskhan
sv10.effect: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.

sv10.name: Tauros
sv10.effect: When it targets an enemy, it charges furiously while whipping its body with its long tails.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Porygon
sv10.effect: It is an artificial Pokémon. Since it doesn't breathe, people are excited by its potential to be useful in any environment.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Porygon2
sv10.effect: This artificial Pokémon evolved thanks to cutting- edge science. It sometimes displays behavior that is not in its programming.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Porygon-Z
sv10.effect: An additional program was installed to create a more advanced Pokémon, but it was apparently flawed. Porygon-Z moves oddly as a result.

sv10.name: Taillow
sv10.effect: It dislikes cold seasons. They migrate to other lands in search of warmth, flying over 180 miles a day.

sv10.name: Swellow
sv10.effect: It dives at a steep angle as soon as it spots its prey. It catches its prey with sharp claws.

sv10.name: Arven's Skwovet
sv10.effect: It stores berries in its cheeks. When there are no berries to be found, Skwovet will stuff pebbles into its cheeks to stave off its cravings.

sv10.name: Arven's Greedent
sv10.effect: If it spots a berry tree, it will immediately go to gather berries without a sideways glance—even if it's in the middle of a battle.

sv10.name: Squawkabilly
sv10.effect: These Pokémon prefer to live in cities. They form flocks based on the color of their feathers, and they fight over territory.

sv10.name: Arven's Sandwich
sv10.effect: Heal 30 damage from your Active Pokémon. If that Pokémon is an Arven's Pokémon, heal 100 damage from it instead. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Power Weight
sv10.effect: The Cynthia's Pokémon this card is attached to gets +70 HP. You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

sv10.name: Emcee's Hype
sv10.effect: Draw 2 cards. If your opponent has 3 or fewer Prize cards remaining, draw 2 more cards. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Energy Recycler
sv10.effect: Shuffle up to 5 Basic Energy cards from your discard pile into your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Ethan's Adventure
sv10.effect: Search your deck for up to 3 in any combination of Ethan's Pokémon and Basic Fire Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Granite Cave
sv10.effect: Steven's Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's) take 30 less damage from attacks from the opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it next to the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

sv10.name: Judge
sv10.effect: Each player shuffles their hand into their deck and draws 4 cards. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Sacred Ash
sv10.effect: Shuffle up to 5 Pokémon from your discard pile into your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Spikemuth Gym
sv10.effect: Once during each player's turn, that player may search their deck for a Marnie's Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into their hand. Then, that player shuffles their deck. You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it next to the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Archer
sv10.effect: You can use this card only if any of your Team Rocket's Pokémon were Knocked Out during your opponent's last turn.  Each player shuffles their hand into their deck. Then, you draw 5 cards, and your opponent draws 3 cards. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Ariana
sv10.effect: Draw cards until you have 5 cards in your hand. If all of your Pokémon in play are Team Rocket's Pokémon, draw cards until you have 8 cards in your hand instead. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Bother-Bot
sv10.effect: Turn 1 of your opponent's face-down Prize cards face up and choose a random card from your opponent's hand. Your opponent reveals that card. You may have your opponent switch those cards. (That Prize card remains face up for the rest of the game.) You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Factory
sv10.effect: Once during each player's turn, if they played a Supporter card that has "Team Rocket" in its name from their hand this turn, they may draw 2 cards. You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it next to the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Giovanni
sv10.effect: Switch your Active Team Rocket's Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Team Rocket's Pokémon. If you do, switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Great Ball
sv10.effect: Flip a coin. If heads, search your deck for an Evolution Team Rocket's Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. If tails, search your deck for a Basic Team Rocket's Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Petrel
sv10.effect: Search your deck for a Trainer card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Proton
sv10.effect: If you go first, you may use this card during your first turn.  Search your deck for up to 3 Basic Team Rocket's Pokémon, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Transceiver
sv10.effect: Search your deck for a Supporter card that has "Team Rocket" in its name, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Venture Bomb
sv10.effect: Flip a coin. If heads, put 2 damage counters on 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. If tails, put 2 damage counters on your Active Pokémon. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Watchtower
sv10.effect: Colorless Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities. You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it next to the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

sv10.name: TM Machine
sv10.effect: Search your deck for up to 3 Pokémon Tool cards that have "Technical Machine" in their name, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Energy
sv10.effect: This card can only be attached to a Team Rocket's Pokémon. If this card is attached to anything other than a Team Rocket's Pokémon, discard this card.  As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides 2 in any combination of Psychic Energy and Darkness Energy.

sv10.name: Yanma
sv10.effect: As Yanma surveys its territory, it periodically stops to hover in place by flapping its wings at high speeds.

sv10.name: Cynthia's Roserade
sv10.effect: The poison in its right hand is quick acting. The poison in its left hand is slow acting. Both are life threatening.

sv10.name: Shaymin
sv10.effect: The blooming of Gracidea flowers confers the power of flight upon it. Feelings of gratitude are the message it delivers.

sv10.name: Crustle
sv10.effect: Its thick claws are its greatest weapons. They're mighty enough to crack Rhyperior's carapace.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Spidops
sv10.effect: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

sv10.name: Hydrapple
sv10.effect: Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.

sv10.name: Rapidash
sv10.effect: The fastest runner becomes the leader, and it decides the herd's pace and direction of travel.

sv10.name: Ethan's Typhlosion
sv10.effect: It has a secret, devastating move. It rubs its blazing fur to cause huge explosions.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Houndoom
sv10.effect: If you are burned by the flames it shoots from its mouth, the pain will never go away.

sv10.name: Blaziken
sv10.effect: When facing a tough foe, it looses flames from its wrists. Its powerful legs let it jump clear over buildings.

sv10.name: Misty's Psyduck
sv10.effect: It is constantly wracked by a headache. When the headache turns intense, it begins using mysterious powers.

sv10.name: Misty's Lapras
sv10.effect: It ferries people across the sea on its back. It may sing an enchanting cry if it is in a good mood.

sv10.name: Clamperl
sv10.effect: Clamperl's pearls are exceedingly precious. They can be more than 10 times as costly as Shellder's pearls.

sv10.name: Electrike
sv10.effect: It stores electricity in its fur. It gives off sparks from all over its body in seasons when the air is dry.

sv10.name: Rotom
sv10.effect: Its electricity-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Orbeetle
sv10.effect: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what's around it—and what's around it can include things over six miles away.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Weezing
sv10.effect: Top-grade perfume is made using its internal poison gases by diluting them to the highest level.

sv10.name: Team Rocket's Murkrow
sv10.effect: Feared and loathed by many, it is believed to bring misfortune to all those who see it at night.

sv10.name: Zamazenta
sv10.effect: Its ability to deflect any attack led to it being known as the Fighting Master's Shield. It was feared and respected by all.

sv10.effect: Its whiskers are essential for maintaining its balance. No matter how friendly you are, it will get angry and bite you if you touch its whiskers.
